documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs, Faculty Affairs
documents.title: Artificial intelligence and academic integrity
documents.summary: A 2023 Faculty Affairs notice from the Office of Academic Affairs on generative AI and academic integrity. It sets a default of no AI unless the course instructor specifically authorizes it, ties this to the Code of Student Conduct, and points to teaching resources and COAM.
documents.stance_why: The statement says generative AI "should not be used in the completion of course assignments unless an instructor ... specifically authorizes their use," so AI is off by default and permission is explicit and per instructor; this is narrower than leaving the choice open, hence restrict.

units.why: The sentence frames generative AI as shaping "the future of work, research and technology" before warning of misuse; it is a rationale (informs), nearest the career type P44 but it is not a learn-AI-for-careers rule.
units.anchor: These tools will help shape the future of work, research and technology
units.frag_start: These tools will help shape
units.fit_note: States AI matters for the future of work, but does not say courses should teach AI use.

units.why: "when used in the wrong way, they can stand in conflict with academic integrity" frames AI misuse as an integrity issue; the reason is honesty, not skill-building, so P95 rather than P41.
units.anchor: when used in the wrong way, they can stand in conflict with academic integrity
units.frag_start: when used in the wrong way

units.why: "complete all academic and scholarly activities with fairness and honesty" binds students under the Code of Student Conduct; the reason given is fairness and honesty, so P95.
units.anchor: complete all academic and scholarly activities with fairness and honesty
units.frag_start: All students have important obligations

units.why: "students are not to use unauthorized assistance ... unless such assistance has been authorized specifically by the course instructor" sets a fallback: assistance is off unless the instructor authorizes it. P06 fits better than P01 because the sentence is about unauthorized assistance in general, not AI by name.
units.anchor: unless such assistance has been authorized specifically by the course instructor
units.frag_start: Specifically, students are not to
units.fit_note: Speaks of unauthorized assistance generally; AI is not named in this sentence.

units.why: "students are not to submit their work without acknowledging any word-for-word use and/or paraphrasing" requires attribution of others' work; it is the general acknowledgment rule next to the AI passage, so P24 with a fit note.
units.anchor: students are not to submit their work without acknowledging
units.frag_start: In addition, students are not to
units.frag_end: work that is not your own.
units.fit_note: General attribution rule for writing, ideas and other work, not AI-specific disclosure.

units.why: "These requirements apply to all students" sets the scope: undergraduate, graduate and professional students are all bound, a scope statement (P56).
units.anchor: apply to all students
units.frag_start: These requirements apply to all students

units.why: "should not be used in the completion of course assignments unless an instructor ... specifically authorizes their use" makes non-use the default with instructor authorization as the exception; a default ban on AI, so P01 (the P06 unit above is the general unauthorized-assistance rule).
units.anchor: should not be used in the completion of course assignments unless an instructor
units.frag_start: To maintain a culture of integrity

units.why: "Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools in the academic setting for specific goals" leaves permission to individual instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools
units.frag_start: Some instructors may approve

units.why: "only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed" requires explicit permission and bounds use to what the instructor allows; closest is P04 (instructor sets the rule), with the explicit-permission requirement as extra.
units.anchor: only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor
units.frag_start: However, these tools should be used
units.fit_note: Adds that permission must be explicit and clear and given by each individual instructor, not just that the instructor decides.

units.why: The page points to "Resources from the Teaching and Learning Resource Center" and the Drake Institute, teaching-support offices; nearest is faculty support (P63) though the pointer says nothing explicit about AI training.
units.anchor: Resources from the Teaching and Learning Resource Center
units.frag_start: Resources from the Teaching and Learning
units.fit_note: A bare link to teaching-center resources; no workshop or advice is described.

documents.unit: Code of Student Conduct (Ohio Admin. Code 3335-23-04)
documents.title: Prohibited conduct, 3335-23-04
documents.summary: The Code of Student Conduct rule on prohibited conduct. Only one clause concerns AI, listing unauthorized generative AI use among examples of academic misconduct; related clauses on course rules apply indirectly.
documents.stance_why: Rule (A)(5) makes "Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence" academic misconduct, implying AI is banned unless authorized; the rule names no permitted uses, so restrict.

units.why: Rule (A)(5) lists "Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence systems or similar technologies to complete academic activities" as an example of academic misconduct, so unauthorized AI use is classified as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence systems or similar technologies to complete academic activities
units.frag_start: (5) Unauthorized use of

units.why: "Students are responsible for reviewing and undertstanding the rules, standards and guidelines provided to them by their academic programs and colleges" makes students responsible for knowing program-level rules (which can include AI rules); general, not AI-specific, hence P78 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for reviewing and undertstanding the rules, standards and guidelines
units.frag_start: Students are responsible for reviewing
units.fit_note: Generic obligation covering any program or college rules; AI not named.

units.why: Misconduct example (1), "Violation of course rules and/or assignment guidelines as contained in the course syllabus", makes breaking a syllabus AI rule misconduct too; a general clause, but the route by which syllabus AI rules are enforced, so P36.
units.anchor: Violation of course rules and/or assignment guidelines as contained in the course syllabus
units.frag_start: (1) Violation of course rules
units.fit_note: General course-rule violation clause; AI is not named.

units.why: The opening says any student who engaged "or attempted to engage" in listed conduct "will be subject to disciplinary action", which reaches attempted unauthorized AI use; it states a consequence without a specific penalty, so P36.
units.anchor: will be subject to disciplinary action by the university
units.frag_start: Any student found to have engaged
units.fit_note: Applies to all prohibited conduct, including attempts; no AI wording.

documents.title: Recommended Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: A Recommended Syllabus Statements document from Undergraduate Education. It supplies a COAM academic misconduct statement and the same AI and academic integrity statement used by Academic Affairs, within a longer list of unrelated syllabus statements that were not coded.
documents.stance_why: The AI section says tools "should not be used in the completion of course assignments unless an instructor ... specifically authorizes their use"; it is offered as a recommended statement, but its content is default restriction with instructor authorization.

units.why: COAM "recommends that every faculty member, instructor, and graduate teaching associate" prepare a syllabus statement on "academic misconduct"; it asks for a syllabus statement, which is P09 (here about integrity in general, with AI in a separate section).
